transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE); Oliver Hayes (CTO, Cobalt Financial), Nina Patel (Head of ML), Samir Aziz (Platform), Rita Gomez (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros and then we'll jump into the Console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdowns.
[00:15] Oliver Hayes: Thanks Maya, excited to see how Redwood surfaces cost at per-route level - that's what we need for the SRE and finance teams.
[00:26] Liam O'Connor: Great. I'll share my screen and walk through the Console. Note: I'm on a slightly laggy connection - apologies if screenshare hiccups.
[00:38] Liam O'Connor: (screen) So first, this is the Usage Analytics landing page. Top-level metrics: tokens generated, embedding units, egress, avg latency, error rate. You can set time ranges, group by model, route, or team.
[00:55] Nina Patel: Can we filter by route and model at the same time? We have a few internal endpoints: chat-v1, summarize-v1, embed-index.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: Yes, you can. Here I select the route filter for "chat-v1" and then the model dropdown for small-llm-2q. The charts recompute and you get per-route latency percentiles and token breakdown.
[01:22] Maya Chen: A useful view is the per-route token cost estimate. It shows prompt vs completion tokens and maps to dollars using your billing profile.
[01:32] Rita Gomez: How accurate is that dollar estimate? We have strict monthly budget buckets.
[01:38] Priya Rao: The Console uses your actual billing rates (hosted or dedicated committed rates). For hosted customers we apply the per-token rate from the account. For Dedicated you can upload committed rates or we show reserved capacity amortization. It's an estimate but aligns within a small margin given the same tokenization model.
[01:52] Samir Aziz: Regarding tokenization, do you account for tokenization differences across models? We use tiktoken-ish tokenizers and saw variation across models.
[02:01] Liam O'Connor: Yes - the token counter is model-aware. It runs the tokenizer used by the selected model family so the prompt/completion split is model-consistent.
[02:10] Oliver Hayes: Can we export per-route cost CSVs to feed into our FinOps tools?
[02:16] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. CSV export or API export. You can schedule daily exports to an S3 bucket.
[02:24] (screen) Now switching to per-route dashboard for chat-v1. On the left we have summary: requests per minute, average tokens per request, 95th p95 latency, error % and cost per 1k requests.
[02:40] Nina Patel: This cost per 1k requests, does it include batching and caching effects? We plan to enable batching at the gateway.
[02:48] Priya Rao: Good question - the console cost estimate assumes runtime observed behavior. If you enable batching and KV prefix caching, the effective tokens billed per request go down and the console will reflect the sampled runtime metrics. For prospective estimates we simulate different batching policies in the Optimize tab.
[03:05] Liam O'Connor: (screen) Here's the timeline view - you can see a spike where the 95th latency jumped and cost briefly increased. Click into the spike to see request samples and the model variant used at that time.
[03:20] Oliver Hayes: That trace view looks helpful for debugging production regressions. Does it tie back to individual API keys or teams?
[03:27] Liam O'Connor: Yes, you can filter by API key, customer team, or route tag. We also show rate limit throttles and retry counts so you can see whether errors were client retries vs server issues.
[03:38] (screen) Now cost breakdown: you can toggle between token-cost view and infra-cost view. Token-cost breaks down by prompt/completion and by model family. Infra-cost shows GPU-hours amortized across models and Dedicated pools.
[03:51] Nina Patel: For Dedicated, how do you account for reserved capacity amortization? We want to know per-route infra chargeback.
[03:58] Priya Rao: We allow you to allocate reserved capacity across routes or teams. The console uses a configurable allocation policy: e.g., proportional to token consumption, or fixed allocation. This gets reflected in per-route infra charge.
[04:13] Samir Aziz: If we move some routes to smaller quantized variants, will the console show a hypothetical cost delta?
[04:20] Liam O'Connor: Yes - in the Optimize area you can run 'what-if' scenarios. Choose a route, select model variants (e.g., 8-bit quantized vs fp16), set batch sizes, and it will estimate token cost and infra cost changes.
[04:31] Oliver Hayes: Nice - can we automate rollouts based on cost-effectiveness thresholds? Like auto-switch to quantized when cost per 1k tokens exceeds X.
[04:40] Priya Rao: There's an A/B rollout feature with automatic fallback policies. We support canary percentages and automated rollback rules based on latency or quality regressions. You can tie the decision to cost signals too.
[04:52] (screen) Next, showing the Alerts and Budget rules. You can set a per-route budget and get Slack/email alerts when estimated spend crosses thresholds.
[05:05] Rita Gomez: For procurement, we need predictable monthly spend. How mature are the budget forecasts?
[05:12] Maya Chen: Forecasts use historical patterns plus optional growth rate assumptions you configure. For conservative planning we recommend Dedicated with committed sizing - then you get predictable infra cost and lower per-token rates.
[05:24] Nina Patel: Security question - we saw references to KMS and audit logs in the docs. For Private deployments we must use our HSM.
[05:33] Liam O'Connor: For Private and Dedicated we support customer KMS/HSM integrations. Audit logs (admin actions, key rotations, API key usage) are exportable and can be forwarded to your SIEM. We have a SOC 2 report summary we can share.
[05:47] Oliver Hayes: Any show-stoppers for us to run a short PoC? Our platform team is worried about VPC peering and egress rules.
[05:55] Priya Rao: We've done several VPC peering setups. Typical items: subnet ACLs, NAT/Egress permissions, and whether you want private link. Samir, if you can share networking constraints we can pre-check and provide a runbook.
[06:09] Samir Aziz: I will - we mostly use strict outbound, need to allow a few Redwood control-plane endpoints and S3 for logs.
[06:17] (screen) Now demoing the Optimize "what-if" flow: picking chat-v1 route, baseline cost, then toggling batching from 1 to 8, enabling prefix KV caching. The simulation shows 28% token-cost reduction and 18% infra reduction.
[06:34] Oliver Hayes: That matches the kind of savings we need to justify the Dedicated spend.
[06:39] Nina Patel: On quality: how do you measure regressions when switching quantized variants?
[06:45] Priya Rao: We tie quality monitoring to eval sets - you can upload a prompt set and expected outputs or key metrics (e.g., ROUGE, classification accuracy). The Console runs comparisons across model variants and surfaces regressions.
[06:59] Liam O'Connor: (screen) Also showing a sample of the model-level latency histogram and a per-token cost waterfall. Note: some transcription here may show K-V cash in older exports (that's a transcriber quirk).
[07:14] Nina Patel: (laughs) we saw that in other calls, K-V cash indeed.
[07:19] Rita Gomez: Procurement question - what are the payment terms and cancellation windows for Dedicated?
[07:25] Maya Chen: Typically monthly invoicing with 30-day net terms for pilot tiers; annual committed contracts for Dedicated with termination clauses. We'll share standard terms and SOW templates.
[07:36] Oliver Hayes: For the PoC, we're aiming to validate three things: 1) cost delta when enabling batching + quantization, 2) latency at p95 under production load, 3) connectivity in our VPC.
[07:48] Priya Rao: Sounds good. We'll scope a 2-week PoC: baseline week collecting metrics, then optimization week running the changes.
[07:56] Samir Aziz: On the technical side, what's the preferred method to run load during the benchmark? We can run our internal load drivers but want to use the same tokenization to match costs.
[08:06] Liam O'Connor: We'll provide a sample load script that uses the same tokenizer and simulates real request shapes. For better fidelity we recommend sharing a sampled traffic trace (anonymized).
[08:17] (screen) Closing with the final recap slide.
[08:22] Maya Chen: Quick recap: we'll send pricing + SOC2 summary, Liam will prepare the PoC checklist and load script, Cobalt will share traffic samples and networking constraints. Proposed PoC window Jan 26-30.
[08:36] Oliver Hayes: That works. One last ask - can you include an export of the per-route breakdown for a sample month? It helps our finance team.
[08:44] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include a sample CSV and an API endpoint you can hit for continuous exports.
[08:50] Rita Gomez: Great, thank you.
[08:52] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the attachments and set the calendar for the PoC kickoff.
[08:59] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-attributions and small OCR-like typos (e.g., K-V cash) - overall medium fidelity.
